study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Both criteria are satisfied: (1) The study clearly states objectives to uncover heterogeneity in mood disorders using individual biomarkers and to link imaging phenotypes with clinical behavior and genetic risk; (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is described to create maturation curves, compute individual deviations, and subtype patients for clinical and genetic characterization and replication.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Uncovering such heterogeneity using neuroimaging-based individual biomarkers, clinical behaviors, and genetic risks, might contribute to elucidating the etiology of these diseases and support precision medicine." | "We applied regional gray matter volumes (GMV) and quantile normative modeling to create maturation curves, and then calculated individual deviations to identify subtypes within the patients using hierarchical clustering."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: NEW model built. Eligibility criteria for HC are described (no recurrent mood disorder/psychotic history; exclusions for substance abuse, neurological disease, MRI contraindications, head injury). Image quality standards are specified via CAT12 IQR thresholds (fail if noise ≤ C and total IQR < B; cutoff ≥80%, ≥ grade B). Final sample sizes are reported (404 HC). Reasons for exclusion are implied by QC criteria but specific counts of exclusions are not reported.
